supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: frontend-external_error z=22198335.64; frontend_latency-90 z=433.22 (2758.4%); currencyservice_latency-50 z=270.73 (1353.7%); checkoutservice_latency-90 z=181.45 (990.5%)
traces for currencyservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 0.15->0.14ms (0.93x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 5.2->74.33ms (14.28x), errors 0.0->0.0008

significant deviations in scope [service=currencyservice]: currencyservice_latency-50 z=270.73 (1353.7%); currencyservice_latency-90 z=110.76 (1569.5%); currencyservice_workload z=-6.78 (-53.9%); currencyservice_cpu z=-3.33 (-35.6%)

alternatives_rejected.why: currencyservice_cpu fell 35.6% (z=-3.33) and own span self-time stayed flat at 0.15->0.14ms (E2, E3), so the service is not compute-bound; the latency is added on the network path.
Inbound errors barely moved (0.0->0.0008) while inbound latency rose 14.28x (E2), which points to delay rather than loss.
Frontend latency and external errors (E1) match frontend waiting on slow currencyservice calls, which show the largest per-service latency deviation (p50 +1353.7%, E1/E3).
checkoutservice latency-90 deviation (z=181.45) is smaller than currencyservice's (z=270.73) (E1), and checkoutservice is a caller of currencyservice, so its slowdown is downstream of it.

proposed_fix.description: Inspect the currencyservice pod's network path, including any tc/netem qdisc, sidecar, or network policy, and remove the injected latency. Then confirm that caller-observed currencyservice latency returns to its roughly 5ms p50 baseline, and roll back any recent network or mesh config change that touched currencyservice.
